title: Pac-Man (Ghost AI)
summary: Four instances of one parameterized Ghost system, a mode scheduler that broadcasts scatter/chase waves to all of them, and a push$/pop$ frightened interrupt that must resume whichever phase it cut off.
teaches: Parameterized multi-instance systems · $OutOfPen HSM parent · push$/pop$ frightened interrupt that resumes the interrupted phase
controls: Arrows/WASD move · power pellets frighten ghosts · SPACE start · P pause · R refill

machines.title: GhostGame — the mode scheduler with a push$/pop$ interrupt
machines.blurb: The global phase clock. Scatter and Chase alternate on a wave schedule ($.phase_index picks the duration); each phase's enter handler broadcasts the change to every ghost. A power pellet push$-es whichever phase is running and transitions to Frightened; when the frighten timer expires (or on frighten_expired), pop$ resumes the exact phase that was interrupted — two callers, two pop targets, and the interrupted phase's timer picks up where it left off.

machines.title: Ghost — one system, four live instances
machines.blurb: Instantiated four times — @@Ghost(name, home_corner, target_kind) for Blinky, Pinky, Inky, and Clyde — so four independent compartment sets run the same generated machine. $Chase and $Scatter are children of the $OutOfPen parent (=> $^ forwards what they don't handle); a power pellet push$-es the current mode and enters $Frightened, and pop$ returns each ghost to whatever it was doing. Eaten ghosts detour through $Eaten back to $InPen. The panel highlights Blinky's instance.

machines.title: GhostPen — the release ladder
machines.blurb: A one-state timer machine: every release_interval seconds it offers the next penned ghost for release, and the scheduler's _try_release() consumes the offer. Deliberately boring — it exists to show a Frame system as a plain component beside the dramatic ones.
